## Close-class correction: superseded (link-backed), not obsolete — avoids force

The `obsolete` close is force-gated: per `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `obsolete`/`wontfix` are reason-only classes that still require a certified plan-review attestation (this triage doc has no implementable plan, so `review-plan` would BLOCK it), leaving only an operator `--force` — which agents must not use.

But `obsolete` was the wrong class anyway. This ticket's requested work **provably landed elsewhere**: the 2-consecutive alarm dampening was delivered under `4557-1f33-7a3f-47c7` (ashen-flirty-kangaroo, "Bridge schedule to hourly"), commit `432a92c1654f`, on `origin/main` since 2026-08-13 — 16 days before this ticket was filed. That is exactly the **link-backed administrative disposition** the close gate is designed for: closing `superseded` against a live replacement link skips the attestation with a verifiable in-tracker fact (not unverifiable operator prose), and records a signed `disposition` verdict — no force, no missing-signature audit gap.

Recorded `4557 supersedes fe28` and closing `superseded`. Disposition and rationale are unchanged from the operator-approved decision (work already shipped; nothing to implement; Option B not pursued).
